newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists to sue prosecutor over party ban.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists to sue prosecutor over party ban.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists said on Thursday they would take legal action against the country's top prosecutor for attempting to close Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party as a threat to the secular order.
"We will bring him to court. He produced unlawful and groundless documents against us," State Minister Abdullah Gul told Reuters.
Top prosecutor Vural Savas said on Wednesday he had filed a case with the constitutional court to outlaw Welfare on the grounds that it endangered the basic tenets of the secularist Turkish state.
On Tuesday Erbakan's government narrowly survived a parliamentary challenge over charges of straying from the secularist path set out at the founding of modern Turkey in 1923.
Legal sources said it could take at least six months for a verdict in any court case aimed at closing Welfare.
Erbakan has upset the secularist elite, led by the army, with plans for limited Islamist reforms since he became NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader in modern times last June.
